reason: 7.0 fits a quiet Blue Zone island with Faros and Armenistis beaches and sea hot springs; the low Q comes from depth 0.02 and recognition 0, a POI coverage gap rather than an appeal error, and the LP mention is a value-for-money list.

Kalemegdan at the Sava and Danube confluence, Knez Mihailova, Saint Sava and Zemun give it more than Monaco (6.0); on a par with Geneva, still below Milan's 7.0 because of the sprawl and traffic Wikivoyage notes.

Two UNESCO sites (Bauhaus Dessau, the Woerlitz Garden Realm), but the town was almost completely destroyed in 1945 and rebuilt in GDR slab; 6.3 is right for a specialist architecture stop, and Woerlitz lies outside the town.

Strong museums, the John Rylands Library, the Town Hall and football lift it well above Birmingham (4.5), while the post-industrial fabric keeps it below Milan; 6.0 holds, and the LP 'learn' list is thematic.
A compact, walkable pink-brick centre with the Capitole, Saint-Sernin and the Canal du Midi is a notch above Belgrade or Manchester and close to Milan; 6.5 slightly undersells it.

Knossos and the Archaeological Museum are world class, but Wikivoyage calls many of the city's developments ugly and ill-planned; 7.0 is right. Catalogue note: the Tripadvisor rank is for Crete the island, which this city row inherits.
The Victorian red-sandstone grid, free Kelvingrove, Mackintosh and the Necropolis put it above Manchester, but closures (the School of Art) and grey edges keep it below Milan; 6.5 holds.

The Frauenkirche, the Zwinger with the Sistine Madonna and the Green Vault on the Elbe justify 7.8; the low Q comes from beauty 0.28 and recognition 0 (the Elbe Valley lost its UNESCO status in 2009), not from appeal.
The Gothic cathedral with exceptional stained glass, San Isidoro, Casa Botines and a free-tapas old town sit just below Carcassonne's 7.5; 7.2 holds.
A small stone old town with Pirin NP access, but Wikivoyage stresses heavy overdevelopment and a beginner-level ski area; 6.0 holds, and the Q of 7.0 already gives a Good band.
Vieux-Port, Notre-Dame de la Garde, MuCEM, Le Panier and the Calanques inside the city limits give it more than Glasgow; 6.8 keeps it below Milan given the uneven whole.
7.0 matches the Milan anchor on the hand scale. Catalogue problem: the row is keyed and named for Malpensa airport, 49 km from Milan in Ferno (Varese); it should be the city of Milan.
Harbourside, the SS Great Britain, Clifton and the gorge bridge offset post-war blight that Wikivoyage calls horrible; 6.8 holds, level with Toulouse and Marseille.
The UNESCO Stari Most, the bazaar and day trips to Blagaj, Pocitelj and Kravica justify 7.5 for a compact old town; Q 7.7 (Very good) is already consistent with the LP listing.

Q 7.9 is not really low. Catalogue note: the appeal reason credits the Tramuntana and the calas, which belong to the island; the city alone (cathedral, Almudaina, Bellver) would sit nearer 7.3, so this row stands in for Mallorca.

A Borghi piu belli village with Isola San Giulio and the UNESCO Sacro Monte di Orta, below Hallstatt (8.3); 7.5 is right. The UNESCO Sacro Monte does support it, so 'none' is a matcher gap; Q 9.4 is lifted by depth 0.99 and recognition 0.95.
The papal palace museum, the Bernini church and Lake Albano views make a pleasant half day from Rome, but it is a smaller draw than Windsor (7.0); its Q 9.2 rests on depth and recognition.

The reason credits Seceda and the Alpe di Siusi, which belong to Val Gardena; the village itself is fairy-tale pretty but should not outrank Hallstatt (8.3). Catalogue note: a valley named after one town, and Wikivoyage does have the guide (St. Ulrich), so 'none' is a matcher gap.

Wikivoyage frames Reykjavik as a small, charming base with sprawling suburbs and puts Iceland's nature as the bigger draw; 8.0 counts the excursions. Catalogue problem: the row is keyed to Keflavik airport, about 50 km from the city.

UNESCO-listed and called some of the most dramatic mountain scenery on the planet; 9.4 is right for the area. Catalogue note: a region labelled with one town (Cortina), and both UNESCO and Wikivoyage support it, so 'none' is a matcher gap.
Charming lanes, the Scaliger castle and the Monte Baldo cable car fit 7.2 among Garda villages; Wikivoyage has the guide, so 'none' is a matcher gap.

The monastery, the Black Madonna and the rock spires are among Catalonia's top sights, so 8.0 holds as a site. Catalogue problem: Wikivoyage describes a mountain and natural park, not a village, so the class should be area; the guide exists, so 'none' is a matcher gap.

Canale di Tenno (Borghi piu belli), the lake and the Varone falls are pretty but minor, with no Wikivoyage guide and no mention on Riva's page; it belongs below Malcesine and Orta. The listed borgo is the hamlet of Canale, not the comune.
A modern frazione of Dorgali founded in the 20th century; the appeal is the Golfo di Orosei coast (Cala Luna, Bue Marino), reached by boat. Catalogue note: a coast named after one village.

Our own reason calls the town drab and Wikivoyage calls it a transport and commercial hub; Ben Nevis, the Jacobite train and Glencoe (further south on the A82) make it a strong base, but 8.2 scores the Highlands, not the town. Catalogue note: a region named after one town.

Isola Bella, Isola Madre and Isola dei Pescatori justify 7.9. Catalogue note: a lake named after one town, and Stresa (about 5,000 people) is a town rather than a village; Wikivoyage covers Stresa, so 'none' is a matcher gap.
Ponta da Piedade, Meia Praia and a colourful old town with a harbour fort fit 7.5, tempered by party crowds; Wikivoyage has the guide, so 'none' is a matcher gap.

The largest Tatra lake, under Rysy, is Poland's top mountain sight, so 8.0 holds as a sight despite crowds of over 50,000 in season. Catalogue problem: it is a lake about two hours' walk from the nearest road, not a village; the class should be area or sight.
Medici forts, Napoleon's exile house and a hill-wrapped harbour make a solid Elba base town at 7.0, level with Windsor; its Q 9.0 comes from depth 0.91, not appeal.

It holds the Koenigssee, St. Bartholomae and part of Berchtesgaden NP; Wikivoyage calls the lake the deepest in the Alps, under walls of about 2,000 m. 7.8 fits, with the village itself a small resort.
